# Standard Library Reference

The maniT standard library is declared in `stdlib/*.mt`. A module is brought in
with `use std::<module>;`, and a function is called as `<module>::<name>(...)`.

**Most of this page is generated, and generated by measurement.** The tables
below the line are produced by `tools/stdlib_census.py`, which reads every
declaration out of `stdlib/*.mt` and then **calls each one on both backends** —
compiling a one-line program per function to LLVM and to T3ISA and recording
which of the two accept it.

That is deliberate, and it is the reason this page was rewritten. The previous
version was hand-written on 8 April 2026 and never revisited: it listed roughly
a third of the surface, omitted everything added since, and — the part that
mattered — said nothing about whether the entries it did list actually existed.
`fmt::` once documented twenty-five functions that were declared in ManiT,
declared in LLVM, and defined nowhere. A reference that lists a name it has not
called is a claim, not a record.

Read the columns as:

| Column | Means |
|---|---|
| **Body** | `ManiT` — written in ManiT, so both backends share one definition. `native` — implemented by the C runtime and by the T3 emulator separately. |
| **Works** | `yes` — a call compiles and links on both backends. `LLVM only` / `T3 only` — one side has no definition. `neither` — nothing implements it. `not probed` — its parameters are a `Vec`, a `Map` or a struct, which this census cannot synthesise. |

**`Works` is a test of existence, not of correctness.** It says a body is
present on both sides, not that the two agree — that is what the differential
tests in `tests/` are for. And `not probed` is an admission, not a pass.

To regenerate after changing the stdlib:

```sh
cargo build --release
python3 tools/stdlib_census.py            # rewrite this file
python3 tools/stdlib_census.py --check    # or just verify it is current
```

## Types with methods

The three sections that follow are hand-written, because their surface is
methods on a type rather than free functions and the census only walks free
functions. Every constructor and method listed was compiled on both backends on
21 August 2026.

## std::sync

Synchronisation primitives for cooperative multitasking.

| Construct | Constructor | Methods |
|-----------|------------|---------|
| `Mutex<T>` | `Mutex::new(initial: T)` | `.lock()`, `.unlock()`, `.get() -> T`, `.set(v: T)` |
| `AtomicTrit` | `AtomicTrit::new(t: trit)` | `.get() -> trit`, `.set(t: trit)`, `.cas(expected, desired) -> bool` |
| `Barrier` | `Barrier::new(n: int)` | `.wait()` — blocks until n tasks have called wait() |
| `Semaphore` | `Semaphore::new(count: int)` | `.acquire()`, `.release()` |

### Usage

```maniT
use std::sync;

// Mutex: protect shared state
let counter: Mutex<int> = Mutex::new(0);
counter.lock();
let v = counter.get();
counter.set(v + 1);
counter.unlock();

// AtomicTrit: lock-free flag
let status: AtomicTrit = AtomicTrit::new(0);
status.set(+);

// Barrier: synchronise N tasks
let b: Barrier = Barrier::new(3);
spawn { do_work_a(); b.wait(); };
spawn { do_work_b(); b.wait(); };
b.wait();   // all three meet here

// Semaphore: rate limiting
let sem: Semaphore = Semaphore::new(2);
sem.acquire();    // at most 2 tasks past here simultaneously
do_critical();
sem.release();
```

## std::async

Async/await cooperative scheduler.

| Function | Signature | Description |
|----------|-----------|-------------|
| `async::yield_now` | `()` | Yield to the scheduler (cooperative preemption point) |
| `async::sleep` | `(ms: int)` | Yield for approximately `ms` milliseconds |
| `async::spawn_task` | `(fn() -> T) -> Task<T>` | Spawn a named function as a task |
| `async::select` | `(task_a: Task, ...) -> T` | Wait for the first task to complete |

`spawn { block }` is syntax sugar for creating and scheduling an anonymous task.
`await task` suspends the current task until `task` completes and returns the value.

### Usage

```maniT
use std::async;

async fn worker(id: int) -> int {
    async::sleep(10 * id);
    id * id
}

fn main() {
    let t1 = worker(1);
    let t2 = worker(2);
    let t3 = worker(3);

    let first = async::select(t1, t2, t3);
    io::println("First result:");
    io::print_int(first);
    io::newline();
}
```

## std::io

Console and stream I/O. Every function here is native, which is why a third of them are missing on one backend or the other — a native is two implementations, and nothing checked that both were written.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `io::eprint` | `(s: str)` | native | **neither** | Print a string without a trailing newline to stderr. |
| `io::eprintln` | `(s: str)` | native | **neither** | Print a string followed by a newline to stderr. |
| `io::print` | `(s: str)` | native | yes | Print a string without a trailing newline to stdout. |
| `io::print_bool3` | `(b: bool3)` | native | yes | Print a bool3 value: displays "True", "Unknown", or "False". |
| `io::print_t9` | `(n: t9)` | native | **neither** | Print a t9 (9-trit) value in balanced ternary notation. |
| `io::print_ternary` | `(n: t27)` | native | **T3 only** | Print a t27 (27-trit) integer in balanced ternary notation. Example output: "+0-+0" for the value 72. |
| `io::print_trit` | `(t: trit)` | native | yes | Print a single trit value: displays "+", "0", or "-". |
| `io::print_tryte` | `(t: tryte)` | native | yes | Print a tryte (3-trit) in balanced ternary notation. |
| `io::println` | `(s: str)` | native | yes | Print a string followed by a newline to stdout. |
| `io::println_bool` | `(b: bool)` | native | yes | Print a bool (true/false) followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_bool3` | `(b: bool3)` | native | yes | Print a bool3 value followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_float` | `(f: float)` | native | yes | Print a float in decimal followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_int` | `(n: int)` | native | yes | Print an integer in decimal followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_t9` | `(n: t9)` | native | **neither** | Print a t9 value followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_ternary` | `(n: t27)` | native | yes | Print a t27 value in balanced ternary followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_trit` | `(t: trit)` | native | yes | Print a trit value followed by a newline. |
| `io::println_tryte` | `(t: tryte)` | native | **T3 only** | Print a tryte value followed by a newline. |
| `io::read_float` | `() -> float` | native | **neither** | Read a line from stdin and parse it as a float. Panics if the input is not a valid float. |
| `io::read_int` | `() -> int` | native | **LLVM only** | Read a line from stdin and parse it as an int. Panics if the input is not a valid integer. |
| `io::read_line` | `() -> str` | native | **LLVM only** | Read a single line from stdin (newline stripped). Blocks until the user presses Enter. |
| `io::stderr` | `() -> Stderr` | native | **neither** | Return the process stderr handle. |
| `io::stdin` | `() -> Stdin` | native | **neither** | Return the process stdin handle. |
| `io::stdout` | `() -> Stdout` | native | **neither** | Return the process stdout handle. |

## std::fmt

Rendering values as text. Four functions are native — `format`, `show_int`, `show_float`, `show_bool` — and the rest are ManiT written over them, so both backends get one body.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fmt::align_center` | `(s: str, width: int, pad: char) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Center `s` in a field of `width` characters.  An odd remainder goes to the right, so align_center("hi", 5, '-') is "-hi--". |
| `fmt::align_left` | `(s: str, width: int, pad: char) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Left-align `s` in a field of `width` characters. |
| `fmt::align_right` | `(s: str, width: int, pad: char) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Right-align `s` in a field of `width` characters, padding with `pad`. Returns `s` unchanged when it is already at least `width` long — it is never truncated. |
| `fmt::ansi_wrap` | `(code: str, body: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Each ESC is built by its own str::from_char call because a `str` local can only be moved once, and this needs two of them. |
| `fmt::balanced_digits` | `(n: int) -> Vec<int>` | ManiT | yes | ManiT's % truncates toward zero, so it yields 2 and -2 where balanced ternary needs -1 and +1; the fix-up is the two `if`s, and the carry is folded into (v - d) / 3 which stays exact for either sign. |
| `fmt::digit_glyph` | `(d: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Glyph for a balanced ternary digit given as an int in {-1, 0, +1}. |
| `fmt::format` | `(template: str, args: [str]) -> str` | native | not probed | Panics if the number of placeholders does not match len(args). |
| `fmt::format1` | `(template: str, a: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convenience: format with a single argument. |
| `fmt::format2` | `(template: str, a: str, b: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convenience: format with two arguments. |
| `fmt::format3` | `(template: str, a: str, b: str, c: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convenience: format with three arguments. |
| `fmt::pow3_int` | `(k: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | A local helper because math::pow3 does not resolve on the T3 backend; see ORACLE_FINDINGS section 17. Keeping it here means this module has no dependency on math:: at all. |
| `fmt::print_section` | `(title: str)` | ManiT | yes | Print `title` centered and surrounded by separator lines. |
| `fmt::print_separator` | `(width: int, ch: char)` | ManiT | yes | Print a horizontal separator line of `width` characters. |
| `fmt::print_truth_table` | `(op_name: str, op: fn(trit, trit: ?) -> trit)` | ManiT | not probed | tand \|  +  0  - -----+--------- + \|  +  0  - 0 \|  0  0  - - \|  -  -  - |
| `fmt::show_binary` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Present for interoperability with binary hardware and file formats.  Base 3 is the native radix of this language — reach for show_t27 or show_dual unless you are talking to something binary. |
| `fmt::show_bool` | `(b: bool) -> str` | native | yes | Convert a bool to "true" or "false". |
| `fmt::show_bool3` | `(b: bool3) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a bool3 to "True", "Unknown", or "False". |
| `fmt::show_dual` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Format `n` as both decimal and balanced ternary side-by-side. Example: show_dual(5) -> "5 (+--)" |
| `fmt::show_float` | `(f: float) -> str` | native | yes | Convert a float to a decimal string (default precision: 6 sig figs). |
| `fmt::show_float_dp` | `(f: float, dp: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Scales by 10^dp into an int, so it is exact only while \|f\| * 10^dp stays inside the int range.  Use show_float or show_float_sci for magnitudes beyond that. |
| `fmt::show_float_sci` | `(f: float) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a float in scientific notation with six decimal places and a two-digit signed exponent, matching C's "%e": show_float_sci(12345.0) is "1.234500e+04".  Zero is "0.000000e+00". |
| `fmt::show_hex` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert an int to hexadecimal ("0x1a2b").  Negatives keep their sign in front of the prefix: show_hex(-26) is "-0x1a". |
| `fmt::show_hex_upper` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert an int to uppercase hexadecimal ("0x1A2B"). |
| `fmt::show_int` | `(n: int) -> str` | native | yes | Convert an int to a decimal string. |
| `fmt::show_octal` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert an int to octal ("0o755"). |
| `fmt::show_t27` | `(n: t27) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a t27 to its balanced ternary string (no leading zeros). |
| `fmt::show_t27_colour` | `(n: t27) -> str` | ManiT | yes | The ESC byte is built with `27 as char` because ManiT string literals have no \x or \u escape — the lexer accepts only \n \t \r \\ \" and \0. |
| `fmt::show_t27_padded` | `(n: t27, width: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a t27 to a zero-padded balanced ternary string of exactly `width` trit positions.  Truncates on the left if the value needs more trits. |
| `fmt::show_t9` | `(n: t9) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a t9 to balanced ternary (no leading zeros). |
| `fmt::show_trit` | `(t: trit) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a trit to "+", "0", or "-". |
| `fmt::show_trit_slice` | `(trits: [trit]) -> str` | ManiT | not probed | Trit slices are stored least-significant-first, and ternary::trits_to_str emits them in that stored order, so this reverses it. Leading zeros are dropped — that is what "compact" means here — but a value of zero still renders as "0". An empty slice gives an empty string. |
| `fmt::show_trit_table` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | pos       3^pos  trit   contribution 2           9     +              9 1           3     -             -3 0           1     -             -1 total                              5 |
| `fmt::show_tryte` | `(n: tryte) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a tryte to balanced ternary (always 3 characters). |
| `fmt::to_radix` | `(n: int, base: int, digits: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | One helper behind show_hex, show_hex_upper, show_octal and show_binary, rather than four separate conversions that can each be wrong in their own way.  `base` must be at least 2 and no more than str::len(digits). |
| `fmt::zero_pad` | `(s: str, width: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | A leading "-" stays in front of the zeros, which is the whole reason this is not just align_right(s, width, '0'): zero_pad("-42", 5) is "-0042", never "00-42". |

## std::str

String inspection and manipulation. The ten primitives are native; the other forty are ManiT over those ten.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `str::byte_len` | `(s: str) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Return the number of bytes in the UTF-8 encoding of `s`. |
| `str::center` | `(s: str, width: int, pad_char: char) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Center `s` within `width` BYTES, padding both sides with `pad_char`.  P48. An odd remainder goes to the right, so center("hi", 5, '-') is "-hi--". |
| `str::char_at` | `(s: str, i: int) -> char` | native | yes | Return the BYTE at position `i` (0-indexed), as an unsigned value 0..=255. Out of range gives 0.  P48: this is a byte, not a codepoint — for "aéb" the four indices give 97, 195, 169, 98. |
| `str::char_count` | `(s: str) -> int` | native | yes | P48: the only function here that does not count bytes, and the one to reach for when the question is "how many characters".  It is not an index — no function in this module takes a codepoint offset. |
| `str::concat` | `(a: str, b: str) -> str` | native | yes | Concatenate two strings. |
| `str::contains` | `(s: str, needle: str) -> bool` | native | yes | Return true if `s` contains the sub-string `needle`. |
| `str::count` | `(s: str, needle: str) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Count non-overlapping occurrences of `needle` in `s`. |
| `str::drop` | `(s: str, n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Return all but the first `n` BYTES of `s`.  Panics if n > len(s).  P48: a byte count, so on a multi-byte character this can split it. |
| `str::ends_with` | `(s: str, suffix: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if `s` ends with `suffix`. |
| `str::find` | `(s: str, needle: str) -> int` | native | yes | Return the BYTE index of the first occurrence of `needle` in `s`, or -1 if not found.  P48. |
| `str::from_bool` | `(b: bool) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a bool to "true" or "false". |
| `str::from_bool3` | `(b: bool3) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a bool3 to "True", "Unknown", or "False". |
| `str::from_char` | `(c: char) -> str` | native | yes | One of only two primitives in this module that touch a char — `char_at` is the other. Every char-dependent function above (to_upper, to_lower, pad_left, pad_right, center) is written in ManiT on top of these two, so each has exactly one implementation and the two backends cannot diverge. |
| `str::from_float` | `(f: float) -> str` | ManiT | yes | The five converters below delegate to fmt:: rather than carrying their own bodies. They are the same conversion under a second name, and one body per conversion is the whole reason `fmt` was moved into ManiT — a second implementation here is precisely how `align_left` came to mean two different things at once (ORACLE_FINDINGS section 14a). |
| `str::from_int` | `(n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert an int to its decimal string representation. |
| `str::from_ternary` | `(n: t27) -> str` | ManiT | yes | MST-first with no leading zeros, so it is the exact inverse of parse_ternary above — verified as a round trip, not assumed. |
| `str::from_trit` | `(t: trit) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert a trit to "+", "0", or "-". |
| `str::is_alpha` | `(s: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if every BYTE of `s` is an ASCII letter.  P48. The empty string is false — see is_numeric. |
| `str::is_alphanumeric` | `(s: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if every BYTE of `s` is an ASCII letter or digit.  P48. The empty string is false — see is_numeric. |
| `str::is_blank` | `(s: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Whitespace is space, tab, newline and carriage return — exactly the four that trim() strips, so `is_blank(s)` and `is_empty(trim(s))` always agree. Vertical tab and form feed are deliberately NOT included: widening the set here would make a string that is blank but does not trim away to nothing. |
| `str::is_empty` | `(s: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if `s` has zero bytes. |
| `str::is_numeric` | `(s: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | The empty string is FALSE here, not vacuously true. Read literally, "every byte is a digit" is true of a string with no bytes, but these three predicates exist to validate input and "" is not a number, a word, or an identifier. is_blank below is the deliberate opposite — "" IS blank — which is why the choice is spelled out on each rather than left to the reader. |
| `str::join` | `(parts: Vec<str>, sep: str) -> str` | ManiT | not probed | The separator goes BEFORE every element except the first, rather than after every element except the last. Both read the same in prose; only the first survives an empty Vec without a trailing separator to strip. |
| `str::len` | `(s: str) -> int` | native | yes | Return the number of BYTES in the UTF-8 encoding of `s`. For the number of characters, see `char_count`. |
| `str::lines` | `(s: str) -> Vec<str>` | ManiT | yes | Split `s` into individual lines (splitting on "\n" and "\r\n"). |
| `str::pad_left` | `(s: str, width: int, pad_char: char) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Pad `s` on the left with `pad_char` until its length is at least `width`. Returns `s` unchanged when it is already at least `width` long. |
| `str::pad_right` | `(s: str, width: int, pad_char: char) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Pad `s` on the right with `pad_char` until its length is at least `width`. Returns `s` unchanged when it is already at least `width` long. |
| `str::parse_float` | `(s: str) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Digits are decoded through `char_at ... as int` rather than the ten-way string comparison parse_int uses. Both work; this one is shorter and is the same primitive to_upper/to_lower are built on. |
| `str::parse_int` | `(s: str) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Parse `s` as a decimal integer.  Panics on failure. |
| `str::parse_ternary` | `(s: str) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Parse a balanced ternary string ("+", "0", "-" characters) as a t27. Ignores leading whitespace.  Panics on invalid characters. |
| `str::repeat` | `(s: str, n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Repeat `s` exactly `n` times, concatenating the copies. |
| `str::replace` | `(s: str, from: str, to: str) -> str` | native | yes | Replace every non-overlapping occurrence of `from` with `to`. |
| `str::replace_first` | `(s: str, from: str, to: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Replace only the first occurrence of `from` with `to`. |
| `str::reverse` | `(s: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Reverse the BYTE order of `s`.  P48: on a multi-byte character this reverses its bytes, which is not a character reversal; see the module header.  Reversing ASCII is exact. |
| `str::rfind` | `(s: str, needle: str) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Return the BYTE index of the last occurrence of `needle` in `s`, or -1 if not found.  P48. |
| `str::slice` | `(s: str, start: int, end: int) -> str` | native | yes | Return a sub-string of `s` from index `start` up to (not including) `end`. |
| `str::split` | `(s: str, delim: str) -> Vec<str>` | native | yes | Split `s` on every occurrence of `delim`, returning a Vec of sub-strings. Consecutive delimiters produce empty strings in the result. |
| `str::split_head` | `(s: str, sep: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Return the substring before the first occurrence of `sep`. Returns the whole string if `sep` is not found. |
| `str::split_tail` | `(s: str, sep: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Return the substring after the first occurrence of `sep`. Returns empty string if `sep` is not found. |
| `str::splitn` | `(s: str, delim: str, n: int) -> Vec<str>` | ManiT | yes | Split `s` into at most `n` parts on `delim`. |
| `str::starts_with` | `(s: str, prefix: str) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if `s` begins with `prefix`. |
| `str::substr` | `(s: str, start: int, n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Return a sub-string of `s` starting at byte offset `start` with length `len`. |
| `str::take` | `(s: str, n: int) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Return the first `n` BYTES of `s`.  Panics if n > len(s).  P48: a byte count, so on a multi-byte character this can split it. |
| `str::to_lower` | `(s: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert all ASCII letters to lowercase. |
| `str::to_upper` | `(s: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Convert all ASCII letters to uppercase. |
| `str::trim` | `(s: str) -> str` | native | yes | Remove leading and trailing ASCII whitespace. |
| `str::trim_chars` | `(s: str, chars: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Remove leading and trailing occurrences of `chars` (any char in the set). |
| `str::trim_end` | `(s: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Remove only trailing ASCII whitespace. |
| `str::trim_start` | `(s: str) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Remove only leading ASCII whitespace. |
| `str::try_parse_float` | `(s: str) -> Result<float, str>` | ManiT | yes | Try to parse `s` as a float. Strict in the same way, and with the same note about Result methods. |
| `str::try_parse_int` | `(s: str) -> Result<int, str>` | ManiT | yes | NOTE for callers: as of 20 August 2026 `Result` supports construction and `match`, but `.unwrap()` and `.is_ok()` are declared in type inference and emitted by NEITHER backend (ORACLE_FINDINGS section 18). Consume the result with `match`, not with a method, until that is fixed. |

## std::math

Arithmetic. Every float function is implemented in ManiT — T3 is ternary hardware with no libm, so a native would have meant writing the function twice. Three balanced-ternary helpers stay native because the T3 emulator answers them directly.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `math::_atan_poly` | `(t: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | atan(t) for \|t\| <= tan(pi/8) = 0.4142 — Taylor through t^47. Successive terms shrink by t^2 <= 0.1716, so the tail after 24 terms is under 9e-21 and no term ever cancels against its neighbour. |
| `math::_cos_poly` | `(r: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | cos(r) for \|r\| <= pi/4 — Taylor through r^18. |
| `math::_cosh_poly` | `(x: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | cosh(x) for \|x\| <= 1 — Taylor through x^18. |
| `math::_pio2_sub` | `(x: float, c2: float, c1: float, c0: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | The split is what makes this work.  A plain Cody-Waite `x - nf*PIO2_1` needs that product to be exact, which holds only while nf carries about 21 significant bits; beyond that the rounding of the product IS the answer. With 21-bit chunks each chunk*piece product is exact by construction (21 bits times a 32-bit constant is 53), the scaling by 2^42 / 2^21 is a pure exponent change, and the twelve exact terms are subtracted in a double-double accumulator by TwoSum, which is also exact. |
| `math::_rem_pio2_ext` | `(x: float) -> [float]` | ManiT | yes | Reduce x (>= 0, < 2^52) modulo pi/2.  Returns [r, q]: r in [-pi/4, pi/4], q the quadrant 0..3 as a float. |
| `math::_sin_poly` | `(r: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | sin(r) for \|r\| <= pi/4 — Taylor through r^15; the first dropped term is below 7e-17 relative. |
| `math::_sinh_poly` | `(x: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | sinh(x) for \|x\| <= 1 — Taylor through x^19.  Every term is positive, so there is no cancellation anywhere; this is what keeps sinh accurate near zero, where (e^x - e^-x)/2 throws away every digit x has. |
| `math::_trig_n` | `(x: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Quadrant count n = nearest integer to x * 2/pi, for 0 <= x < 2^21. sin/cos/tan reduce \|f\| and restore the sign afterwards, so this never sees a negative argument and no sign branch is needed. |
| `math::_trig_r` | `(x: float, nf: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | pi/2 is carried as PIO2_1 + PIO2_2 + PIO2_3 + PIO2_3T, which reproduces it to 160 bits.  PIO2_1/2/3 each have at most 32 significant bits, so nf*PIO2_k is an EXACT product while \|nf\| < 2^21, and x - nf*PIO2_1 is then exact by Sterbenz.  That exactness is the whole reason the reduction survives large arguments; a single-constant `x - n*PI2` loses one digit per decade of x. |
| `math::abs` | `(n: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Absolute value of an integer. |
| `math::acos` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::asin` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::atan` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::atan2` | `(y: float, x: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::balanced_round` | `(f: float, trit_position: int) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Example: balanced_round(3.7, 1) -> 3.0   (nearest multiple of 3¹ = 3) balanced_round(7.1, 1) -> 9.0   (nearest multiple of 3¹ = 9 > 6) |
| `math::cbrt` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Cube root (cbrt).  Exact for perfect cubes when input is a whole number. Cube root (cbrt).  Exact for perfect cubes when input is a whole number. |
| `math::ceil` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Ceiling — smallest integer not less than f. Ceiling — smallest integer not less than f. |
| `math::clamp` | `(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Clamp n to the inclusive range [lo, hi]. |
| `math::cos` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::cosh` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::div_near` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | native | yes | Ties go away from zero rather than to even because the balanced system is symmetric about zero and `div_near(-a, b) == -div_near(a, b)` is the property worth keeping; the unbiasedness balanced ternary claims comes from the representation, not from the tie-break. |
| `math::div_trunc` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | native | yes | Truncating division — the quotient rounded towards zero. v1's `/`. |
| `math::exp` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | e^f. e^f. |
| `math::exp2` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | 2^f. 2^f. |
| `math::exp3` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | 3^f — ternary exponential, exact for integer f. 3^f - ternary exponential, exact for integer f. |
| `math::fabs` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Absolute value of a float. Absolute value of a float. |
| `math::factorial` | `(n: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Reach differs by backend and cannot be made not to: 20! needs 64 bits, so on T3 (27 trits) this is exact only to n = 15. |
| `math::fclamp` | `(f: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Clamp f to the inclusive range [lo, hi]. Clamp f to the inclusive range [lo, hi]. |
| `math::floor` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Floor — largest integer not greater than f. Floor — largest integer not greater than f. |
| `math::fmax` | `(a: float, b: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Larger of two floats. Larger of two floats. |
| `math::fmin` | `(a: float, b: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Smaller of two floats. Smaller of two floats. |
| `math::fpow` | `(base: float, exp: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Raise base to floating-point exponent. Raise base to floating-point exponent. |
| `math::fract` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Fractional part of f (f - trunc(f)). Fractional part of f (f - trunc(f)). |
| `math::from_balanced_ternary` | `(trits: [trit]) -> int` | native | not probed | Reconstruct an integer from a balanced ternary trit array (LST-first). |
| `math::gcd` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Greatest common divisor (always non-negative). |
| `math::hypot` | `(a: float, b: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Hypotenuse: sqrt(a² + b²) without intermediate overflow. Hypotenuse: sqrt(a² + b²) without intermediate overflow. |
| `math::is_pow3` | `(n: int) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if n is a perfect power of 3. |
| `math::isqrt` | `(n: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | The comparison is `mid <= n / mid`, not `mid * mid <= n`. They decide identically, but the squaring form builds products far larger than the result and TRAPS on T3 for inputs whose answers are perfectly representable. |
| `math::lcm` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Divides BEFORE multiplying. The textbook `abs(a * b) / gcd(a, b)` forms an intermediate larger than the answer, and on T3 that traps: lcm(2000000, 3000000) is 6000000, comfortably in range, while a*b is 6e12 and is not. |
| `math::log` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Natural logarithm (base e). Natural logarithm (base e). |
| `math::log10` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Base-10 logarithm. Base-10 logarithm. |
| `math::log2` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Binary logarithm (base 2). Binary logarithm (base 2). |
| `math::log3` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Ternary logarithm (base 3) — native to maniT. log3(27.0) == 3.0 exactly. Ternary logarithm (base 3) - native to maniT. log3(27.0) == 3.0 exactly. |
| `math::logn` | `(f: float, base: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Logarithm to an arbitrary base. Logarithm to an arbitrary base. |
| `math::max` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Larger of two integers. |
| `math::min` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Smaller of two integers. |
| `math::pow` | `(base: int, exp: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | The `if e > 0` guard on the squaring is load-bearing, not an optimisation. A T3 int is 27 trits and TRAPS on overflow, so squaring `b` one last time after the final multiply — which the textbook loop does — can trap on an input whose answer is perfectly representable. The guard keeps \|b\| <= \|result\| at every step, so pow overflows only when its own result does. |
| `math::pow3` | `(n: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Raise 3 to integer exponent — trivially cheap in balanced ternary. pow3(n) == 3^n. |
| `math::rem_near` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | native | yes | The balanced remainder pairing with div_near — `a - div_near(a, b) * b`. Lies in [-\|b\|/2, +\|b\|/2], so unlike rem_trunc it can be negative for a positive `a`: `div_near(7, 2)` is 4 and `rem_near(7, 2)` is -1. v2's `%`. |
| `math::rem_trunc` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | native | yes | The remainder pairing with div_trunc. Takes the sign of `a`. v1's `%`. |
| `math::round` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Round to nearest integer, half-away-from-zero. Round to nearest integer, half-away-from-zero. |
| `math::sign` | `(n: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Sign of n: returns +1, 0, or -1 as an int. Note: the trit equivalent is trit_sign in std::ternary. |
| `math::sin` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::sinh` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::sqrt` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Square root. Square root. |
| `math::tan` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::tanh` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | — |
| `math::tdiv` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Checked deliberately rather than assumed: a symmetric digit set invites round-to-nearest, but the doc says truncation and tests/23_t3isa_instructions.mt independently pins the T3 ISA's `/` to it (-10 / 3 == -3). Round-to-nearest would be a different function, not this one. |
| `math::tmod` | `(a: int, b: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Written as the identity itself so it holds by construction rather than by coincidence. (It equals `a % b`; that was verified, not assumed.) |
| `math::to_balanced_ternary` | `(n: int) -> [trit]` | native | yes | (Both worked examples here were wrong until 19 August 2026: the first was a draft left mid-correction in the comment, and the second gave [-, +, -], which is -1 + 3 - 9 = -7. Verified against both backends.) |
| `math::to_degrees` | `(rad: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Convert radians to degrees. Convert radians to degrees. |
| `math::to_radians` | `(deg: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Convert degrees to radians. Convert degrees to radians. |
| `math::trit_count` | `(n: int) -> int` | native | yes | Number of trits required to represent n in balanced ternary. trit_count(0) == 1, trit_count(1) == 1, trit_count(13) == 3. |
| `math::trit_weight` | `(n: int) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Return the ternary digit sum: sum of the absolute values of each trit. Equivalent to the Hamming weight for balanced ternary. |
| `math::trunc` | `(f: float) -> float` | ManiT | yes | Truncate toward zero. Truncate toward zero. |

## std::ternary

The balanced-ternary core. Mixed: the primitives the backends lower directly stay native, and everything built on top of them is ManiT.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ternary::count_nonzero_trits` | `(val: t27) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Count the number of non-zero trits in val. |
| `ternary::highest_trit_pos` | `(val: t27) -> int` | ManiT | yes | Return the most significant non-zero trit position (0-indexed from LST). Returns -1 for the value zero. |
| `ternary::int_to_t27` | `(n: int) -> t27` | native | yes | Convert a plain int to t27, wrapping if the value is out of range. |
| `ternary::int_to_t9` | `(n: int) -> t9` | native | yes | Convert int to t9, wrapping on overflow (range: -9841..9841). |
| `ternary::int_to_trit` | `(n: int) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | The doc comment said "panics for other values" until 19 August 2026 and neither backend did that: the T3 emitter treated it as an identity register move, so int_to_trit(5) yielded 5 -- not a valid trit at all -- while LLVM clamped. That is why it was one of the four DIVERGENT functions. Clamping to the sign is what every caller in the tree already relied on. |
| `ternary::int_to_trits` | `(n: int, width: int) -> [trit]` | native | yes | Convert an int to a trit slice of exactly `width` trits (LST-first). Trits beyond `width` are discarded; missing positions are zero-padded. |
| `ternary::int_to_tryte` | `(n: int) -> tryte` | native | yes | Convert int to tryte, panicking if out of range. |
| `ternary::is_negative_trit` | `(val: t27) -> bool` | ManiT | yes | Return true if the value is negative in balanced ternary sense (MST is -). |
| `ternary::pack_t9` | `(trits: [trit]) -> t9` | ManiT | not probed | Pack up to 9 trits into a t9. |
| `ternary::pack_trits` | `(trits: [trit]) -> t27` | native | not probed | Pack a slice of trits (LST-first, i.e. index 0 = least significant trit) into a t27.  If the slice has fewer than 27 elements the remaining positions are filled with 0.  Panics if the slice has more than 27 trits. |
| `ternary::t27_and` | `(a: t27, b: t27) -> t27` | native | yes | Bitwise (trit-wise) AND of two t27 values: min per position. |
| `ternary::t27_explain` | `(val: t27)` | ManiT | yes | Display a t27 in a human-readable table showing each trit position and its contribution to the total value.  Writes to stdout. |
| `ternary::t27_from_str` | `(s: str) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Parse a balanced ternary string ("+", "0", "-" chars) into a t27. Ignores leading whitespace.  Panics on invalid characters. |
| `ternary::t27_from_t9` | `(hi: t9, mid: t9, lo: t9) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Build a t27 from three t9 segments (high, mid, low). |
| `ternary::t27_from_trits` | `(trits: [trit; 27]) -> t27` | ManiT | not probed | Build a t27 directly from a 27-element trit array (LST-first). |
| `ternary::t27_neg` | `(a: t27) -> t27` | native | yes | Trit-wise negation of a t27: flip sign of every trit. |
| `ternary::t27_or` | `(a: t27, b: t27) -> t27` | native | yes | Trit-wise OR of two t27 values: max per position. |
| `ternary::t27_to_int` | `(val: t27) -> int` | native | yes | Convert t27 to int (sign-extended; preserves negative values). |
| `ternary::t27_to_str` | `(val: t27) -> str` | native | yes | Format a t27 as a balanced ternary string using "+", "0", "-" characters. Leading zero trits are suppressed (except for the value zero itself). Example: t27_to_str(5t) -> "+--"  (since 9-3-1 = 5) |
| `ternary::t27_to_str_padded` | `(val: t27) -> str` | ManiT | yes | Format a t27 as a fixed-width 27-character string (with leading zeros). |
| `ternary::t27_xor` | `(a: t27, b: t27) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Trit-wise XOR (addition mod 3, balanced) of two t27 values. |
| `ternary::t9_to_int` | `(val: t9) -> int` | native | yes | Convert a t9 to int. |
| `ternary::trit_add` | `(a: trit, b: trit) -> (trit, trit)` | ManiT | yes | Add two trits.  Returns (sum_trit, carry_trit). The full-add truth table follows balanced ternary carry rules. trit_add(+, +) -> (-, +)  because +1 + +1 = +2 = -1 + 1*3^1 trit_add(+, -) -> (0, 0)  because +1 + -1 = 0 |
| `ternary::trit_and` | `(a: trit, b: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Ternary AND (Łukasiewicz / min): min(a, b) in {-1, 0, +1}. |
| `ternary::trit_median` | `(a: trit, b: trit, c: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Consensus / median of three trits (used in fault-tolerant TMR logic). Returns the "majority vote" trit. |
| `ternary::trit_mul` | `(a: trit, b: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Multiply two trits.  Result is always a single trit (no carry needed). trit_mul(+, +) -> +    (+1 * +1 = +1) trit_mul(+, -) -> -    (+1 * -1 = -1) trit_mul(-, -) -> +    (-1 * -1 = +1) trit_mul(0, _) -> 0    (0 times anything is 0) |
| `ternary::trit_neg` | `(t: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Negate a trit (ternary NOT): + <-> -, 0 stays 0. |
| `ternary::trit_or` | `(a: trit, b: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Ternary OR (max): max(a, b) in {-1, 0, +1}. |
| `ternary::trit_rotate_left` | `(val: t27, n: int) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Rotate a t27 value left by `n` trit positions. |
| `ternary::trit_rotate_right` | `(val: t27, n: int) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Rotate a t27 value right by `n` trit positions. |
| `ternary::trit_shift_left` | `(val: t27, n: int) -> t27` | native | yes | Left-shift a t27 value by `n` trit positions (multiply by 3^n). Trits shifted beyond position 26 are discarded (wrapping behaviour). |
| `ternary::trit_shift_right` | `(val: t27, n: int) -> t27` | native | yes | Right-shift a t27 value by `n` trit positions (divide by 3^n, truncate). |
| `ternary::trit_sign` | `(t: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Return the sign of a trit as a trit (identity function, included for symmetry with math::sign). |
| `ternary::trit_to_int` | `(t: trit) -> int` | native | yes | Convert a trit to its integer equivalent: + -> +1, 0 -> 0, - -> -1. |
| `ternary::trit_unit` | `(n: int) -> t27` | ManiT | yes | Return a t27 whose value is 3^n (the "ternary unit" at position n). Positions outside 0..26 return 0: 3^27 is outside the 27-trit range and forming it would trap on T3. |
| `ternary::trit_xor` | `(a: trit, b: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Ternary XOR (addition mod 3, mapped to balanced representation). trit_xor(+, -) -> 0   (+1 + -1 mod 3 = 0) trit_xor(+, 0) -> +   (+1 + 0  mod 3 = +1) trit_xor(+, +) -> -   (+1 + +1 mod 3 = -1, i.e. 2 -> -1 in balanced) |
| `ternary::trits_to_str` | `(trits: [trit]) -> str` | native | not probed | Format a trit slice as a string (MST-first for readability). |
| `ternary::tryte_from_trits` | `(t2: trit, t1: trit, t0: trit) -> tryte` | native | yes | Pack exactly 3 trits into a tryte. |
| `ternary::tryte_to_int` | `(t: tryte) -> int` | native | yes | Convert a tryte to int (range: -13..13). |
| `ternary::tryte_to_trits` | `(t: tryte) -> (trit, trit, trit)` | ManiT | yes | Unpack a tryte into its three constituent trits (MST-first order). |
| `ternary::unpack_t9` | `(val: t9) -> [trit` | native | yes | Unpack all 9 trits of a t9. |
| `ternary::unpack_trits` | `(val: t27) -> [trit` | native | yes | Unpack all 27 trits of a t27 into a fixed-size array, LST-first. |

## std::bridge

Binary/ternary interop — packing trits into bytes and back.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bridge::binary_to_t27_pair` | `(bits: [trit; 54]) -> (t27, t27)` | ManiT | not probed | Pack a 54-bit binary array into a pair of t27 values (high 27 bits, low 27 bits). This enables storing a binary-encoded word in two native ternary registers. Each bit occupies one trit position (digit 0 or +1) of its t27. |
| `bridge::binary_to_word` | `(bits: [trit; 54]) -> t27` | ManiT | not probed | If any two-bit pair is the invalid (1,1) pattern, the corresponding trit position is set to 0 (safe fallback).  For strict validation, check each pair with is_valid_encoding() before calling this function. |
| `bridge::bits_to_trit` | `(b1: trit, b0: trit) -> trit` | ManiT | yes | Use is_valid_encoding() to check for the invalid (1,1) pattern before calling this function if error detection is required. |
| `bridge::byte_to_tryte` | `(b: t9) -> tryte` | ManiT | yes | Reads the lowest 6 trit positions of the t9, interpreting each consecutive pair as a trit encoding per bits_to_trit(). Positions [8..6] are ignored. |
| `bridge::is_valid_encoding` | `(b1: trit, b0: trit) -> bool3` | ManiT | yes | In the two-bit-per-trit scheme, (1,1) has no corresponding trit value. This function allows callers to detect corruption or encoding errors at the binary-ternary boundary before conversion. |
| `bridge::t27_pair_to_binary` | `(hi: t27, lo: t27) -> [trit` | native | yes | Unpack a pair of t27 values (high, low) back into a 54-bit binary array. |
| `bridge::trit_to_bits` | `(t: trit) -> (trit, trit)` | ManiT | yes | The returned tuple (b1, b0) uses trit values 0 and +1 to represent binary 0 and 1 respectively, since maniT has no native bit type. |
| `bridge::tryte_to_byte` | `(ty: tryte) -> t9` | ManiT | yes | The pair IS lossless in the direction that matters: all 27 trytes survive `tryte_to_byte` then `byte_to_tryte`, measured on both backends. Scanning all 256 bytes through `byte_to_tryte` then `tryte_to_byte` and finding 232 that do not round-trip is NOT evidence of a defect — 229 of them are not valid encodings at all (27 values cannot have 256 distinct encodings) and the other 3 are the canonical encodings above 255. |
| `bridge::validate_binary_buffer` | `(bits: [trit; 54]) -> bool3` | ManiT | not probed | This is the fast-path check for incoming binary data at the binary-ternary bridge boundary. |
| `bridge::word_to_binary` | `(w: t27) -> [trit` | native | yes | This is the format expected by binary DMA, PCIe, or USB bridges described in Claim 17. |

Full-width multiplication needs a double-word intermediate the language does not have on T3. |

Requires b > 0 (this module divides only by 3 and 19683). |

## std::env

## std::test

Assertions. Pure ManiT over `io::println` and `env::exit`, so it needs nothing from the C runtime and works identically on both backends. The condition is `bool3`, not `bool`: `tand`, `tor` and comparisons against `unknown` produce a genuine three-valued answer, and an assertion that cannot tell `false` from `unknown` reports a verdict it does not have. Hence three entry points — `assert`, `assert_unknown`, `assert_false` — one per trit.

| Function | Signature | Body | Works | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test::assert` | `(cond: bool3, msg: str)` | ManiT | yes | Assert that `cond` is TRUE (+1). `unknown` and `false` both fail, and are reported separately. |
| `test::assert_false` | `(cond: bool3, msg: str)` | ManiT | yes | Assert that `cond` is FALSE (-1) -- definitely false, not merely not-true. |
| `test::assert_unknown` | `(cond: bool3, msg: str)` | ManiT | yes | Assert that `cond` is UNKNOWN (0) -- that the question is genuinely undecided. There is no binary equivalent of this assertion; it is the one that makes a three-valued logic testable at all. |
| `test::fail` | `(kind: str, msg: str)` | ManiT | yes | Print an assertion failure and terminate with a non-zero exit status. Separated from `assert` so every entry point below reports identically. |
| `test::pass` | `()` | ManiT | yes | The passing arm. `tif` arms are expressions, so each of the three needs something to evaluate; this is the nothing. |

## Census

**331 declarations** across 13 modules: **231 call cleanly on both backends**; 37 were not probed (their parameters are types this census cannot synthesise — a `Vec`, a `Map`, a struct); and **63 do not work on at least one backend**.

The *Works* column records whether a one-line program calling the function compiles and links on each backend. It is a test of existence, not of correctness: a function marked `yes` has a body on both sides, which is exactly what `fmt::`'s twenty-five documented-but-undefined entries did not. A `not probed` row is an admission, not a pass.
